question: Which federal changes has the research found but not yet written up as recorded changes?
answer: 18 federal changes, dated September 17, 2026 to September 22, 2026, have been researched with a before and after and an official source but are not yet written up in the movement registry. Among them: FY2026 standardized rating and performance-award controls (Office of Personnel Management); Polysilicon anti-stockpiling import gate (Bureau of Industry and Security); Fort Carson and Pinon Canyon withdrawal extension PLO 7971 (Bureau of Land Management); Temporary moratorium on certain ACA Marketplace agent and broker registration (Department of Health and Human Services and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services). The research accepted all 18; each card prints its review decision and what the record does not prove.

sections.sub: Grouped by subject area. Open a card for the dates on record, who acted and the review decision.

uncertain: The current movement vocabulary cleanly covers authority through operation, delivery, effect, source custody and return gates, but it does not cleanly type court adjudication, congressional procedure, oversight findings or internal organization changes.
Do not force-fit those object classes into an existing stage. Add typed stages only after method review, or explicitly keep those classes outside the movement lane.
'Accepted' means the research kept the change for write-up. It is not yet a recorded change with a stage on the ladder.
A date is the date the official record shows. Effective dates after the research cutoff are still future or conditional.

catalog_context.title: One map to browse all saved federal research
catalog_context.answer: This is a navigation hub, not a finding: it puts Katie's saved government research, a map of federal bodies, congressional committees, confirmed changes and known gaps in one place, while keeping each source's evidence separate.

catalog_context.title: What changed on federal websites, September 16–22
catalog_context.answer: Separate agencies changed who could qualify, access records, receive payments or carry out programs. No single government-wide program appeared, and announcements, payments, delivery and measured effects still require separate proof.
